source.section: The Basics: Prime and Composite Numbers

problem.text: Let $p$, $q$, and $r$ be prime numbers such that $2pqr+p+q+r=2020$. Find $pq+qr+pr$.

steps.title: Where to start: look at even and odd
steps.body: When an equation involves primes, a good first question is whether any of them is $2$, the only even prime. Here $2pqr$ is always even and $2020$ is even, so the parity of $p + q + r$ is forced.

your_turn.prompt: If $p$, $q$, $r$ were all odd, would $2pqr + p + q + r$ be even or odd?
your_turn.answer: Odd, because even plus the sum of three odd numbers is odd. That cannot equal $2020$.

steps.title: Exactly one prime is $2$
steps.body: So at least one prime is $2$. If exactly two were $2$, then $p + q + r$ would be $2 + 2 + \text{odd}$, which is odd again. If all three were $2$, the left side would be only $22$. So exactly one prime is $2$, and since the equation and $pq + qr + pr$ are symmetric, we can say $p = 2$.

your_turn.prompt: Put $p = 2$ into the equation and simplify.

steps.title: Factor with Simon's trick
steps.body:
The left side almost factors. Simon's Favorite Factoring Trick means adding a constant so a product appears. Multiply both sides by $4$ and add $1$:
$$(4q+1)(4r+1) = 4\cdot 2018 + 1 = 8073$$

your_turn.prompt: Expand $(4q+1)(4r+1)$ to check that this really matches the equation.

steps.title: Search the factor pairs
steps.body: Now $8073 = 3^3\cdot 13\cdot 23$. We need to split it into two factors that each leave remainder $1$ when divided by $4$, and then $q = \tfrac{\text{factor} - 1}{4}$ and $r$ must both be prime. The pairs are $1\cdot 8073$, $3\cdot 2691$, $9\cdot 897$, $13\cdot 621$, $23\cdot 351$, $27\cdot 299$, $39\cdot 207$ and $69\cdot 117$.

your_turn.prompt: Test the pairs $9\cdot 897$ and $13\cdot 621$. Do they give primes?
your_turn.answer: No. $9\cdot 897$ gives $q = 2$ and $r = 224$, and $13\cdot 621$ gives $q = 3$ and $r = 155 = 5\cdot 31$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: Pairs with $3$, $23$, $27$ or $39$ fail because those leave remainder $3$ when divided by $4$, and $1$ would give $q = 0$. The pair that works is $117 = 3^2\cdot 13$ and $69 = 3\cdot 23$, giving $q = 29$ and $r = 17$, both prime. Then $pq + qr + pr = 58 + 493 + 34 = 585$. The answer is **$585$**.
